title: Sausage & Cheddar Egg Muffins
subtitle: grab-and-go baked egg cups with mild sausage, onion and old cheddar
imageAlt: Golden baked egg muffins studded with sausage and cheddar on a cream plate, one split open, with a navy napkin
servingsNote: 12 egg muffins: 2 each, a week of breakfasts for two

beforeYouStart.text: Grease the muffin tin well, or use silicone cups, so the eggs release cleanly.
Squeeze the sausage meat out of the casings.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and brush a 12-cup muffin tin well with the melted butter.

steps.title: Sausage
steps.text: Brown the sausage meat and onion in a skillet over medium-high, breaking it up, 8–10 minutes, until no pink remains and it reads 71°C (160°F). Drain on paper towel.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk the eggs, milk, salt, pepper and garlic powder in a large measuring jug.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Divide the sausage and cheddar among the cups, then pour in the eggs until each is ¾ full.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 20–22 minutes, until puffed, set in the centre and 74°C (165°F). Cool 5 minutes, then run a knife around each and lift out.

fixIt.fix: Grease more heavily, or use paper liners sprayed with oil.
Drain the sausage well and don't add raw watery vegetables.
That's normal; they sink as they cool. Don't overbake or they turn rubbery.

saleTip: Buy the big sausage pack on sale; use half here and freeze the rest for burritos.
swap: Diced ham or crumbled bacon for sausage. Mozzarella for cheddar.
leftovers: Keep in a container lined with paper towel; reheat two for breakfast.
doneness: Sausage meat to 71°C (160°F); egg dishes to 74°C (165°F) in the centre (Health Canada).
source: Based on tested baked egg muffin methods (Budget Bytes, Canadian Living): cooked filling in a greased muffin tin, topped with whisked eggs and baked at 175°C until set.
prepAhead: Cook the sausage up to 2 days ahead.
Baked muffins freeze up to 2 months.
reheat: Microwave 2 muffins 45–60 seconds (from frozen 1½–2 minutes), until 74°C (165°F).
airFryer: Bake in silicone muffin cups in the air fryer at 150°C (300°F) for 12–15 minutes, until set and 74°C (165°F). Reheat cold ones at 160°C (325°F) for 4–5 minutes.

basic.note: Sausage, egg and cheddar; no onion or garlic powder.

stepNotes.1: Basic: brown the sausage on its own.

fancy.note: Add crisp bacon and diced tomato for a 'loaded' egg muffin.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: first cook the bacon in the skillet 6–8 minutes until crisp, drain and crumble, then brown the sausage.
stepNotes.3: Fancy: add bacon and tomato with the cheddar.

why.1-2: A little milk keeps the eggs tender instead of rubbery.
why.0-0: Pre-cooking the sausage drains its fat so the muffins don't go greasy.

funFact: Canadian hens lay about 9 billion eggs a year, roughly 240 for every person in the country.

keeps.note: freeze on a tray, then bag

drink: Coffee or tea; a smoothie on busy mornings.
